title: Dhuhr, the midday prayer
tomorrow: which prayer does the Qur'an single out by name: guard it?

lines: IN THE MIDDLE OF THE RUSH?
cards: Twelve-thirty in a coffee shop: milk screaming in the steam wand, the grinder roaring, a line to the door. In the back, behind the sacks of beans, a prayer rug is rolled against the wall.

When Dhuhr comes in, the owner, Amira's dad, hands the register over for a few minutes and goes. Some regulars have stopped noticing. The ones who notice ask the same thing: in the middle of the rush?

teach.b: Dhuhr is the prayer just after the sun passes its height. It lands in the loudest part of the day, and the way in is through the senses.
First, water. The Qur'an asks for washing before prayer: the face, the hands and arms to the elbows, a wipe of the head, the feet. That's wudu.

In a report in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ says that when a believer washes the face, the faults the eyes took in leave with the water. At noon, cool water on hot wrists is the first thing that changes. Second, heat.

teach.h: HEAT: WAIT FOR IT TO COOL.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari he tells people that when the heat is fierce, they may wait to pray Dhuhr until it cools. He knew what midday feels like; he didn't pretend the sun wasn't there. Third, rest.
When the time for prayer came, he would say to Bilal, the caller, in a report kept by Abu Dawud: give us rest by it. Not get it over with.
Rest. So the noise stays in the front room, the water runs cold, the forehead touches the floor, and for a few minutes the day stops asking for anything. Then back to the register.

how: Dhuhr is prayed after the sun passes its height, before 'Asr. Muslims at work or school make wudu and pray in an office corner, a back room or a campus prayer space; on Fridays the Jumu'ah prayer takes its place for those who attend.

o: the prayer said as the sun touches the horizon
the prayer said just after the sun passes its height
a short pause taken only on hot summer days

games.q: noon, by the senses — tap the pairs.

s: the Prophet once told people they could delay Dhuhr until the heat eased
in Sahih al-Bukhari: when the heat is fierce, wait for it to cool.
the Prophet spoke of prayer as a duty to get over with
he said to Bilal: give us rest by it.
Dhuhr is said just after the sun passes its height
the midday prayer, landing in the loudest part of the day.

games.q: a scorching summer noon. the courtyard is blazing, and the people at the mosque wait a while before praying Dhuhr. why?
o: the Prophet allowed waiting for fierce heat to cool.
Dhuhr can't be prayed in summer until near sunset.
they're just late; Dhuhr belongs at the stroke of noon.
games.why: in Sahih al-Bukhari, when the heat is fierce, he said to wait until it cools. the prayer still comes before 'Asr; the senses are taken seriously.

practice: If there's a tap or a cold glass near you, run cool water over your wrists, or hold the glass against them, for a few seconds. Then sit, hands open on your knees, and follow where the coolness stays and where it fades.
Let whatever's urgent wait in the next room.

wordCard.voice: Dhuhr: the midday prayer, just after the sun passes its height, entered through cool water, prayed in the middle of the noise.
